sections.content:
Whoa. Clicked the gray piece, then clicked the red target → the red piece moved from (24-29,18-21) to (30-33,12-17)! The gray piece didn't move. So clicking the red target toggles the red piece regardless of which piece you clicked first??
Wait, let me re-verify. Before this action: red piece at (24-29,18-21), gray at (30-33,8-11). After: red at (30-33,12-17), gray still at (30-33,8-11). So the red piece toggled back to the 4x6 slot.
Hmm! So maybe the "click the piece first" requirement doesn't exist at all. Maybe clicking the target always toggles that color's piece! Let me re-verify the history:
- t8: clicked red target (clicked red piece at t4, t7). Red toggled.
- t10: clicked blue target (clicked blue piece at t9). Blue/checkerboard swapped.
- t18: clicked red target (clicked red piece at t17). Red toggled.
- t22: clicked blue target (clicked blue piece at t21). Blue/checkerboard swapped.
- t24: clicked red target (clicked red piece at t23). Red toggled.
- t26: clicked blue target (clicked blue piece at t25). Swapped.
- t28: clicked blue target (clicked checkerboard at t27). Swapped.
- t34: clicked red target (clicked gray at t33). Red toggled!
So in every case, clicking the target toggled the piece — the prior click may have been irrelevant! The target click alone might toggle the piece.
But wait, t12: clicked red piece (26,19) — no effect (piece clicks do nothing). t13: clicked checkerboard — nothing. t14: clicked blue — nothing. t15: clicked red — nothing. So piece clicks do nothing, target clicks toggle the piece.
So the mechanic is simply: click the red target → red piece toggles between two slots. Click the blue target → blue piece and checkerboard swap.
Then, when did the red pedestal disappear? At t8, when the red piece moved to (24-29,18-21). The red piece is now back at (30-33,12-17), and the red pedestal is still gone.
So the pedestal is a latch: it disappeared when the red piece was in (24-29,18-21).
For the blue pedestal: the blue piece was in (34-37,8-11) at t26 (and the checkerboard too at t28). The pedestal didn't disappear.
So the latch condition isn't "the piece is in the near slot."
What else happened at t8? Let me look at the full diff of t8 again: the red pedestal (W→B) disappeared, and the red piece moved. 128 cells. The pedestal is 3x9=27 cells plus the T's outline... actually, the diff showed the pedestal region (16-18,44-52) and the T's boundary cells (17,52), (19,41-44,52-55), (20,41,55), (21,41,55), (22,41-55) → all W→B. So the entire red T + pedestal turned black?? No wait — the T is red (R), and the diff showed W→B at those positions. Let me re-read the t8 diff:
(16,44-52) W→B: top of pedestal.
(17,44) W→B, (17,52) W→B: pedestal sides.
(18,44) W→B, (18,52) W→B.
(19,41-44) W→B, (19,52-55) W→B: T's top bar outline?
(20,41) W→B, (20,55) W→B.
(21,41) W→B, (21,55) W→B.
(22,41-55) W→B: T's bottom bar.
Hmm, so the white outline around the red T disappeared. The T itself (red) remains. So the red T had a white outline/border, and that disappeared!
Looking at the initial image: the red T at the top right — is there a white outline? Looking at the first image... the red T appears to have a white border around it (the "pedestal" I described was actually a white outline around the T, not a pedestal below it!).
Yes! Looking at the first image again: the red T has a white outline around the entire T shape. The blue T also has a white outline. So the "pedestal" = the white outline around the T.
At t8, the red T's white outline disappeared (the T became "solid"/"activated").
So the goal is: make both T's solid (remove the white outline).
The red T's outline disappeared when the red piece moved to (24-29,18-21) (t8).
The blue T's outline is still there. The blue piece moved to (34-37,8-11) at t26 — no effect on the outline.
So what's the difference between the red piece at (24-29,18-21) and the blue piece at (34-37,8-11)?
Red T: rows 17-21, columns 42-54. Red piece at (24-29,18-21).
Blue T: rows 34-38, columns 42-54. Blue piece at (34-37,8-11).
Hmm, the blue piece's rows (34-37) match the blue T's rows (34-38) more closely than the red piece's rows (24-29) match the red T's rows (17-21). So it's not row alignment.
Maybe the outline disappears when the piece is in a slot that's adjacent to a room?
- Red piece at (24-29,18-21): adjacent to room A (18-23,22-27)? Corner contact only.
- Blue piece at (34-37,8-11): edge-adjacent to room B (38-43,8-13).
No.
Maybe the outline disappears when the piece is in a slot that's adjacent to another piece of the same color family?
- Red piece at (24-29,18-21): below is the dark red 4x4 at (30-33,18-21) — edge-adjacent! Above is the blue at (20-23,18-21).
- Blue piece at (34-37,8-11): above is the gray at (30-33,8-11), below is room B.
So when the red piece was at (24-29,18-21), it was adjacent to the dark red (same color family). When the blue piece was at (34-37,8-11), it was adjacent to the gray (different family).
Hypothesis: the T's outline disappears when the piece is adjacent to a same-color-family piece!
For the blue T: the blue piece needs to be adjacent to the checkerboard (blue family). The blue's slots: (20-23,18-21) and (34-37,8-11). The checkerboard is in the other slot. They're never adjacent (the slots are far apart).
Hmm, no. Unless the checkerboard can be in a different position.
Wait, wait. Let me reconsider. What if the checkerboard isn't part of the blue system, and the "swap" I observed was actually the blue piece moving to (34-37,8-11) and the checkerboard... hmm, no, the checkerboard clearly moved to (20-23,18-21).
Let me re-verify: at t28, I clicked the checkerboard at (21,19) (which was at (20-23,18-21)), then clicked the blue target. Result: the checkerboard moved to (34-37,8-11), and the blue moved to (20-23,18-21). So the checkerboard also responds to the blue target.
So the blue system has two pieces that swap. The red system has one piece that toggles between two slots.
What's the difference between the systems? The red piece's two slots: (24-29,18-21) [6x4] and (30-33,12-17) [4x6]. The blue pieces' slots: (20-23,18-21) and (34-37,8-11) [both 4x4].
The red piece changes shape (4x6 ↔ 6x4) when it toggles! It's a rotation!
The blue piece doesn't change shape (4x4 stays 4x4).
Hmm, so what makes the red T's outline disappear?
Let me try: put the red piece back at (24-29,18-21) (click the red target), and see if the red T's outline comes back (i.e., is it a latch or a toggle).
If the outline comes back, then the outline state = f(piece position), and I need to figure out the correct position for the blue.
If the outline stays gone, it's a latch, and the blue needs some other trigger.
Let me test.
